paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and Tensile Property of Al3Zr/Al-Cu-Ni-V Composite Prepared by In Situ Reaction

evidence.quote: the high-temperature stable D0 23-Al3Zr was introduced to an Al-Cu-Ni-V alloy to improve the HT (350 /C176C) mechanical properties by the melt in situ reaction.

the as-cast microstructure of the composites consists of a-Al, Al 2Cu, Al 3Ni, Al 7Cu4Ni, Al3CuNi, Al 3Zr, and Al 10V phases.
The Al-Al 2Cu eutectic regions having an elliptic morphology are sporadically scattered in the Al-matrix (spot 2 in Fig. 3).
the as-cast microstructure of the composites consists of a-Al, Al 2Cu, Al 3Ni, Al 7Cu4Ni, Al3CuNi, Al 3Zr, and Al 10V phases.
The Al 7Cu4Ni (spot 4) phase has the morphology of a short stick.
The Al 3CuNi (spot 3) phase has the morphology of an interconnected network.
The size of the Al 3Zr phase is in the range of 2-4 lm. The Al3Zr crystals with a tetragonal D0 23 structure are usually produced in the as-cast composite (Ref 44).
A small number of Al 10V phase precipitates (spot 7) are also sporadically distributed in the matrix.
the h¢-Al2Cu precipitations in the composites are more than that in the matrix alloy (Fig. 10a), and the size of h¢-Al2Cu precipitation is slightly reduced as a whole (approximately 200-300 nm).

the T6 heat-treated specimens contain the Al 3Zr phase. TEM SAD analysis in Fig. 13(a) and (c) shows that these particles are D0 23-Al3Zr phases with tetragonal lattice unit cells. The T6 heat treatment has not changed the crystal structure of Al 3Zr but has increased the dissolved Cu and Ni in it, as seen in Fig. 13(e), so it is more suitable to express it in the form of Al 3(Zr, Cu, Ni).
